parts.text: Silver chloride is an ionic compound and is insoluble in water. Molten silver chloride breaks down during electrolysis. The products are chlorine and silver. Chlorine gas is soluble in water and toxic. A student suggests using the apparatus shown to break down silver chloride.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Draw an arrow on the diagram to show where heat must be applied so that the silver chloride can break down. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text: an arrow pointing to the bottom of the test tube.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Complete the diagram to show how chlorine gas can be collected and the volume of the chlorine measured. Label any apparatus you have drawn. [2]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
apparatus that looks like a gas syringe in approximately horizontal orientation connected to delivery tube
graduations shown OR labelled as (gas) syringe

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
any 2 from:
•
yellow / green gas
•
bubbles / effervescence
•
shiny liquid / metal / solid / deposit / substance
max 2

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The person doing the experiment followed all normal laboratory safety rules. State one additional safety precaution that should be taken when doing this experiment. Give a reason for your answer. safety precaution ........................................................................................................................ reason ........................................................................................................................................ [2]
